Surah al-Muddaththir

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Jabir narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I was on Mount Hira, when I was called: 'O Muhammad, you are the Messenger of Allah.' I looked to my right and to my left, but I saw nothing. Then I looked up, and there he was, sitting on a throne between the heaven and the earth—meaning the angel who had called to me. I was terrified and returned to Khadijah, and said: 'Wrap me up, wrap me up!' So Khadijah wrapped me up. Then Jibril came and recited: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾."

That is: al-Mutalaffif bi-thiyabihi (the one wrapped in his garments), from al-Dithar (al-dithār, the outer garment), which is everything of clothing that is worn above the shi'ar (al-shi'ar, the garment that lies directly against the body). Its original form is al-Mutadaththir, which was assimilated (fa-udghima).

"Arise" (qum) from your resting place, or arise with the resolve and determination of one who is firm.

﴿And warn﴾: warn your people of the punishment of God if they do not believe; or carry out the warning without restricting it to any particular person. It is said: he heard from Quraysh what he disliked, so he grieved and covered himself with his garment, pondering as the grieved person does. So it was said to him: O you who turn away the harm of the disbelievers from yourself by wrapping yourself in your garment, arise and occupy yourself with warning, even if the wicked harm you.

(p-562) ﴿And your Lord, glorify⁠﴾. He singled out your Lord for takbir (takbir), which is magnification (al-ta'zim). That is: do not magnify anyone else in your eyes. And say, when anything from other than Allah overwhelms you: "Allahu Akbar" (Allah is greatest). It is narrated that when it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allahu Akbar," and Khadijah said "Allahu Akbar," and she rejoiced and became certain that it was the revelation (al-wahy). It may also be understood as referring to the takbir of the prayer (takbir al-salah). The fa' (fa) has entered with the meaning of a condition (shart), as if it were said: "Whatever the case, do not abandon its takbir."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 4:

﴿And your garments, purify﴾, with water, from impurity (najasah), because prayer is not valid without it, and it is preferable outside of prayer as well. Or: ﴿then shorten﴾, in opposition to the Arabs in their lengthening of garments and trailing of their skirts, since with that one is not safe from contact with impurity. Or: purify yourself from what is loathsome of deeds. It is said, "So-and-so has pure garments" (ṭāhir al-thiyāb) when they describe him as free from blemishes, and "So-and-so has defiled garments" (danis al-thiyāb) of the treacherous person. And because whoever purifies his inner self, his outer self becomes pure outwardly.

**﴿And the abomination﴾**, with a *ḍamma* on the **راء** (*rāʾ*), is read by Yaʿqūb, Sahl and Ḥafṣ. Others read it with a *kasra*: **الْعَذَاب** (*al-ʿadhāb*), meaning "the punishment." What is intended is that which leads to it.

**﴿So abandon﴾**, i.e., persist in abandoning it, because he (the Prophet) was free of it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 6:

﴿And do not bestow, seeking to receive more﴾, with the verb in the nominative (tastakthiru, with a damma), and it is in the accusative position of its grammatical site (mahall) as a circumstantial clause (hal). That is: do not give while seeking more, seeing what you give as abundant, or seeking more than what you have given. For you are commanded with the most noble of characters and the most excellent of manners. It derives from "manna 'alayhi" (to bestow a favour upon him), meaning when one confers a benefit upon someone. And al-Hasan recited "tastakthir" with a sukun, as a response (jawab) to the prohibition (nahy).

﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾: that is, for the sake of the face of Allah, persevere in patience with regard to His commands and His prohibitions, and with regard to everything that must be endured and everything from which one must restrain oneself.
﷼﴿Then when the trumpet is sounded﴾ — the Trumpet is blown, and it is the first blast. It is also said: it is the second.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 74, verse 9:

﴿That﴾: a reference to the time of the *naqr* (the blast on the trumpet), and it is the *mubtada'* (subject, the inchoative of the nominal sentence),

﴿on that day﴾: in the nominative case by position, an *badal* (apposition) to "that" (ذَلِكَ),

﴿is a difficult day﴾: the *khabar* (predicate). It is as if it were said: "So the day of the *naqr* is a difficult day." The *fa'* (ف) in "فَإذا" (then when) indicates *tasbib* (causation), and the *fa'* in "فَذَلِكَ" indicates *jaza'* (consequence/recompense). It is as if it were said: "Be patient over their harm, for before them is a difficult day, on which they will encounter the consequence of their harm, and you will encounter the consequence of your patience with it." The governing element (*'amil*) of "فَإذا" is what the *jaza'* (conditional sense) implies, that is: "So when the trumpet is blown, the matter becomes difficult."

"upon the disbelievers, [it will be] not easy."

The commentator stresses it by saying "not easy" (ghayr yasir), to indicate that it is easy for the believers, or that it is a hardship that is not hoped to become easy, as the difficult matters of this world are hoped to be made easy.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 11:

﴿Leave me with the one whom I created﴾, i.e., leave him to Me, meaning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who was called among his people "al-Wahid" (the Unique). "Man khalaqtu" (the one whom I created) is either conjoined (ma'tuf) or in the accusative as an object "ma'a" (accompanying): ...

﴿alone﴾ (wahidan) is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of the ya' in "dharni" (leave me), meaning: leave me alone with him, for I will suffice you in his affair; or it is a circumstantial qualifier of the ta' in "khalaqtu" (I created), meaning: "I created him alone, no one shared with Me in his creation"; or it is a circumstantial qualifier of the omitted ha' (the pronoun object), or of "man" (the one), meaning: I created him solitary, without family or wealth, and then I bestowed favours upon him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 12:

﴿And I bestowed upon him abundant wealth﴾, spread out, plentiful, or "extended through growth." He had crops, livestock (ḍarʿ), and trade. It is related from Mujahid (Mujahid ibn Jabr): "He had a hundred thousand dinars." And it is related from him that he had land in al-Ta'if whose produce never ceased.

"And sons present with him" (wa-banina shuhudan): present with him in Mecca, since they were wealthy enough not to need to travel. They were ten, and among them who embraced Islam were Khalid, Hisham, and Ammara.

And (﴿I spread out for him [wealth and] provision, spreading it out [abundantly]﴾)... 

Wait, I must translate the given text exactly. Here it is:

"﴿And I made [life] smooth for him, smoothing it [for him]﴾, and I extended for him [his] standing and leadership, and I completed My blessing upon him in both blessings, standing and wealth; and the combination of the two is perfection in the view of the people of this world."

Then he desires that I should increase (him further)? This is a expression of astonishment and disapproval at his greed and eagerness: that is, he hopes that I will increase him in his wealth and his children, without gratitude. Al-Hasan (al-Basri) said: "that I should increase" means that I would admit him into Paradise and grant him wealth and children, as he said: ﴿Surely I shall be given wealth and children﴾.

Translation:

﴿Nay!﴾ A rebuke to him and a cutting off of his hope, meaning: after today, there shall not be combined for him disbelief and an increase in blessings. So after the revelation of the verse, he continued in decline in wealth and standing until he perished.

﴿Indeed, he was stubborn toward Our verses﴾: obstinate (mu'anid), denying (jahid). This is a reason (ta'lil) for the rebuke, given in the form of a resumed statement (isti'naf), as if someone had said: "Why is he not given more?" So it was said: "Indeed, he denied the signs of the Benefactor, and by that he disbelieved His blessing, and the disbeliever does not deserve an increase."

(p-564) ﴿Sa-urhiquhu﴾: I will overwhelm him (sa-ughashshihi), i.e., I will cover him over.

﴿Ṣa'ūdan﴾: an arduous ascent (ʿaqabah shāqqat al-mașʿad), a steep climb that is hard to ascend. And in a hadith: "As-ṣaʿūd (the ascent) is a mountain of fire; one climbs up it for seventy autumns, then falls down from it, and so on forever."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 18:

﴿Indeed, he reflected﴾: an explanation (ta'lil) for the threat (wa'id). It is as if Allah (Exalted is He) hastened to punish him with poverty and humiliation after wealth and honour, because of his obstinacy, and will punish him in the Hereafter with the most severe torment, because he reached the furthest point of obstinacy and named the Qur'an "magic." The meaning is that he reflected on what he would say about the Qur'an.

﴿And he prepared﴾: he arranged in his own mind what he would say and got it ready.

﴿Then he was killed﴾: cursed (lu'ina).

﴿How he calculated﴾: an expression of wonder at his calculation (ta'jib min taqdirihi).

Translation:

﴿Then woe to him, how he calculated﴾. He repeated it for emphasis, and "then" (thumma) indicates that the second curse is more emphatic than the first.
"Then he looked" (thumma naẓara), at the faces of the people, or at what he had devised (fi-ma qaddara).

Then he frowned: he contracted his face.

And he scowled: he increased in the contraction and grimacing.

Then he turned back, (away from the truth),

and was arrogant, (toward it), or (toward) its station; and in his statement: "Then he looked" is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to "he thought and he measured" (fakkara wa-qaddara), and the supplication (al-duʿāʾ) is an interjection (iʿtirāḍ) between the two. And the use of "then" (thumma) among the conjoined items is to clarify that there is a delay (tarākhī) between the conjoined verbs.

﴿So he said: "Indeed, this is"﴾, meaning: what is this?

﴿"only magic that is transmitted (yu'thar)"﴾. It is related from the magicians. It is narrated that al-Walid said to the Banu Makhzum: "By God, I have just heard from Muhammad a speech that is neither the speech of humans nor the speech of jinn. Indeed it has sweetness, and indeed its outer surface has beauty; its upper part is fruitful, and its lower part is abundant with water. It rises and nothing rises above it." The Quraysh said: "By God, al-Walid has apostatized (sabaʾa)!" Abu Jahl, who was his nephew, said: "I will suffice you against him." So he sat beside him, grieved, and spoke to him in a way that angered him. Then al-Walid stood up and came to them and said: "You claim that Muhammad is possessed (majnun). Have you seen him choke (yukhniqu)? You say he is a soothsayer (kahin). Have you ever seen him foretell (yatakahhan)? You claim he is a poet (shaʿir). Have you ever seen him engage in poetry (yataʿatá shiʿran)? You claim he is a liar (kadhdhab). Have you ever caught him in any lie?" They said to all of this: "No, by God." Then they said: "So what is he?" He thought, then said: "He is nothing but a magician. Have you not seen him separate a man from his wife, his son, and his clients (mawali)? And what he says is nothing but magic transmitted from Musaylima and the people of Babylon." The assembly erupted in joy, and they dispersed, marveling at him.

The mention of the fāʾ (فَ, "then") in ﴿فَقالَ﴾ indicates that this word came to his mind and he uttered it without delay.

Translation:

﴿This is nothing but the word of a human being﴾. He did not mention a conjunction (al-'atif) between these two clauses, because the second functions as an emphasis (tawkid) of the first.

﴿I will burn him﴾: I will cause him to enter (the Fire).

Ba­dal (substitute, i.e. apposition) of "سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُودًا" (sa-urhiquhu ṣa'ūdan, "I will overwhelm him with a steep climb").

﴿Saqar﴾: an 'alam (proper noun) for Jahannam (Hell). It is not declined, because of ta'rif (definiteness) and ta'nith (feminine gender).
"And what will make you know what Saqar is?" — an expression of the magnitude of its dread.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 28:

﴿It leaves nothing﴾, meaning: it leaves no flesh,

﴿and spares nothing﴾, [meaning it leaves no] bone. Or: it leaves nothing within it that remains except that it destroys it, and it does not leave it in a state of destruction, but it returns as it was.

The verse is 74:29, and the passage gives grammatical and lexical notes on it.

﴿Lawwaha﴾ (scorching, blackening) is the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada'), meaning: "It is scorching."

﴿lil-bashar﴾: the plural of "bashara," which is the outer surface of the skin. That is, it blackens the skins and burns them.

"Over it" — over Saqar.

"Nineteen" — meaning: nineteen angels are in charge of it, according to the majority (al-Jumhur). It was also said: a category of angels; it was said: a row (saff); and it was said: chiefs (naqib).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 31:

﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire﴾, i.e., its guardians,

﴿except angels﴾, because they are of a different kind from those who are punished, so compassion and tenderness do not overtake them, for they are the mightiest of creation in might; each one of them possesses the strength of both jinn and humankind.

﴿And We have not made their number﴾, nineteen,

﴿except as a trial﴾, i.e., a test and an examination,

﴿for those who disbelieve.﴾ So much so that Abu Jahl said, when the verse "﴿Over it are nineteen﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 30]" was revealed: "Can not each ten of you overpower one of them, and you are the numerous?!" Abu al-Ashadd, who was of severe strength, said: "I will suffice you against seventeen of them; so suffice me, you, against two." Then this was revealed: ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels﴾, i.e., We have not made them men of your kind who could be overcome. They have said, regarding the specification of the guardians by this number, although numbers are not usually sought to have reasons: "Six of them lead the disbelievers to the Fire, six drive them, and six strike them with iron maces, and the remaining one is the guardian of Hell, who is Malik, and he is the chief." It has also been said: "In Saqar there are nineteen levels (darak), and an angel has been set over each level." And it has been said: "It is punished therein with nineteen kinds of punishment, and over each kind is an angel assigned." And it has been said: "Hell is guarded by the same means by which the earth is guarded from the mountains, and they are nineteen, and its original number was one hundred and ninety, except that others branch off from them."

﴿That those who were given the Book may be certain﴾, because their number is nineteen in both Books; so when they hear the like of it in the Qur'an, they become certain that it is sent down from Allah.

﴿And that those who believe may increase in faith﴾, in Muhammad, and this is coordinated with "that those who were given the Book may be certain" (ʿaṭf).

﴿in faith﴾, because of their affirmation of this, just as they affirmed the rest of what was sent down; or: they may increase in certainty by the agreement of their Book with the Book of those others.

﴿And that those who were given the Book and the believers may not doubt﴾. This is also a coordination (ʿaṭf), and in it is an emphasis on certainty and an increase of faith, since certainty and the increase of faith both indicate the absence of doubt. Then it is coordinated, also, with "that he may be certain": ﴿And that those in whose hearts is disease﴾, hypocrisy,

﴿and the disbelievers﴾, and the polytheists, say. If you say: hypocrisy appeared in Medina, and the surah is Meccan, I say: its meaning is: "and that the hypocrites who will appear in the future in Medina, after the Hijrah, and the disbelievers in Mecca, may say:"

﴿What did Allah intend by this as an example?﴾ This is a report of what will be, like the other reports of unseen matters, and this does not contradict the surah being Meccan. It has also been said: the intended meaning of "disease" is doubt and suspicion, because most of the people of Mecca were doubters. "A parable" (mathalan) is a specification (tamyīz) for "this", or a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl) from it, like His saying: ﴿This is the she-camel of Allah, a sign for you﴾ [Hud: 64]. And since the mention of the number is extremely strange, and such a number is worthy that riders carry it as proverbs, it was called a parable. The meaning: "What did Allah intend by this wondrous number? And what meaning did He intend in making the angels nineteen, not twenty?" Their purpose was to deny it altogether, and that it is not from Allah; and that if it were from Allah, it would not have come with this deficient number.

﴿Thus Allah leads astray whom He wills﴾. The kāf is in the accusative position, and "thus" refers to what precedes it of the meaning of misguidance and guidance, i.e., like that mentioned misguidance and guidance, meaning the misguidance of the hypocrites and the polytheists, so that they said what they said, and the guidance of the believers through their affirmation and their seeing the wisdom in that: Allah leads astray whom He wills of His servants, and He is the One who knows in him the choice of error,

﴿and guides whom He wills﴾, and He is the One who knows in him the choice of guidance. In this is evidence for the creation of acts, and for describing Allah with guidance and misguidance. (p-567) When Abu Jahl—may Allah curse him—said: "Does the Lord of Muhammad have helpers other than nineteen?", this was revealed: ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord﴾, because of their great multitude,

﴿except Him﴾. So it is not difficult for Him to complete the guardians to twenty, but for Him in this specific number is a wisdom that you do not know.

﴿And it is not﴾, connected to the description of "Saqar", and "it" refers to it, i.e., Saqar and its description are not

﴿except a reminder to humankind﴾, i.e., a reminder to humankind; or its referent is the verses which were mentioned in it.

﴿Kallā﴾ (By no means), a denial, after He made it (the Qur'an) a reminder, that it should be a reminder for them, because they do not take heed.

﴿Wal-qamari﴾ (And by the moon), He swears by it, on account of the greatness of its benefits.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 33:

﴿And by the night when it retreats﴾. Nafi', Hafs, Hamzah, Ya'qub and Khalaf read "idhā dabara" (when it departs), while the others read "idh adbara" (when it retreats). "Dabara" and "adbara" carry the same meaning, and both mean: it turned its back and went away. It is also said that "adbara" means it turned back and passed on, while "dabara" means it came after the day (i.e., it came after the daytime).
"By the dawn when it brightens" (﴿وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا أَسْفَرَ﴾), i.e., when it shines forth. The answer to the oath (جَوَابُ القَسَمِ) follows:

Indeed it (inna-ha), Saqar (inna Saqar),

﴿is surely one of the greatest (calamities)﴾, al-Kubar being the plural of al-Kubra. That is, it is one of the greatest calamities or the greatest of misfortunes. The meaning of it being "one of them" (ihda-hunna) is that among them it is a single one in magnitude, having no equal, just as you say, "He is one of the men (ahad al-rijal)," and "She is one of the women (iḥda al-nisa')."

"Warner" (nadhīran) is a tamyīz (specification) following "one of" (iḥdā), meaning: indeed it is one of the greatest calamities in warning, just as you say, "She is one of the women in chastity." And [the phrase] "to mankind" (lil-bashar) is a badal (substitution/apposition) from it.

Translation of the passage:

﴿For whoever among you wills﴾, by repeating the preposition (lil-), [it is] ﴿to advance﴾, toward good, ﴿or to hold back﴾, from it. And from al-Zajjaj: toward what he was commanded, or away from what he was forbidden.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 38:

﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾. It is "rahinah" (in pledge, feminine), not the masculine "rahin" as in His saying: ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾ [al-Tur: 21], and this is because of the feminine gender of "nafs" (soul). For if you intended the adjective, it would be said "rahin", since "fa'il" in the sense of "maf'ul" is used equally for the masculine and the feminine. Rather, it is a noun in the sense of "al-rahn" (the pledge), like "al-shatimah" in the sense of "al-shatm" (the insult). It is as if it were said: every soul, for what it has earned, is a pledge. The meaning is: every soul is a pledge, through its earning, before Allah, not released.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 39:

﴿Except the companions of the right hand﴾ That is: the children of the Muslims, for they have no deeds by which they are held in pledge. Or: except the Muslims, for they have freed their necks through obedience, just as the one who pledges redeems his pledge by paying the debt.

(p-568) ﴿In gardens﴾, i.e., they are in gardens whose description cannot be fully comprehended,

﴿they will ask one another﴾ ﴿about the guilty﴾, one of them asking another about them; or "they will ask one another" means others asking them about them.

(p-568) ﴿In gardens﴾, i.e., they are in gardens whose description cannot be fully comprehended,

﴿they will ask one another﴾ ﴿about the guilty﴾, one of them asking another about them; or "they will ask one another" means others asking them about them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 42:

﴿What has brought you into Saqar?﴾ — i.e., "what caused you to enter it" (أدْخَلَكم فِيها).

It might be objected that his saying "What has brought you into Saqar?" does not correspond to his saying "They ask one another about the criminals," since the question here is addressed to the criminals, whereas "They ask one another about the criminals" is a question about them. This correspondence would hold only if it were said: "They ask the criminals: What has brought you into Saqar?" Because "What has brought you into Saqar?" is not an explanation of the asking about them; rather, it is a report of the words of those who are asked about them. The ones being asked relay to the askers what passed between them and the criminals, saying: "We said to them: What has brought you into Saqar? They said: We were not among those who prayed." The text has been abbreviated, as is the manner of the Qur'an. It has also been said that the particle "ʿan" (عَنْ, "about") here is superfluous (زائِدَةٌ).
﴿They will say, "We were not of those who prayed."﴾ That is: we did not believe in its being obligatory.
"And we did not use to feed the poor" (Qur'an 74:44). That is, the way the Muslims feed (the poor).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 45:

﴿And we used to plunge into vain talk along with those who plunged in.﴾ "Al-khawd" (plunging, engaging deeply): beginning in falsehood, meaning we would speak falsehood and lies concerning the signs of Allah.

"And we used to deny the Day of Judgment."

[Al-Nasafi:] "And we used to deny the Day of Recompense", meaning the Reckoning and the Requital.
﴿Until there came to us the certainty﴾, that is, death.

ّ﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾, from among the angels, the prophets and the righteous, because intercession is for the believers and not for the disbelievers. And in it is evidence for the establishment of intercession for the believers, in the hadith: "Indeed, among my community is one who will enter Paradise through his intercession more than the tribes of Rabi'ah and Mudar."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 74, verse 49:

﴿Why then do they turn away from the reminder﴾, from the admonition (al-tadhkir), which is advice (al-'izah), i.e., the Qur'an,

﴿turning away﴾, turning their backs (muwalliyin). It is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring back to the pronoun (al-damir), like the phrase: "What is wrong with you standing?" (ma laka qa'iman).

﴿As if they were﴾ asses, i.e., wild asses, a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to the pronoun in "turning away" (muʿriḍīn),

﴿startled⁽¹⁾﴾, extremely fleeing, as if they sought flight from themselves. With a fatḥah on the fāʾ, it is read by Medina and Syria, meaning: something else startled them.

(p-569)

Notes on the translation:
1. Mustanfirah: the form (with kasrah on the fāʾ) denotes animals that flee in extreme panic; the reading with fatḥah (mustanfarah) is the passive, "driven to flight by another."

﴿They fled from a lion﴾: [فَرَّتْ مِن قَسْوَرَةٍ]. Here *ḥāl* (circumstantial qualifier) is in the accusative, and *qad* (قَدْ) is with it, with an implied element accompanying it. *Al-qaswarah* (القَسْوَرَةُ) means archers, or it means lion. It is on the pattern *fa'lah*, derived from *al-qasr* (القَسْر), which is compulsion and overpowering, and the people are likened, in their turning away from the Qur'an and from listening to the Reminder, to donkeys that bolted in their flight.

Qur'anic quotation (74:52): "Nay, but every man among them desires that he be given scrolls spread out."

Scrolls (qarativs) that are unrolled and read. The reason is that they said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "We will not follow you until you bring each one of us books from heaven, bearing the heading: 'From the Lord of the worlds to so-and-so son of so-and-so, in which we are commanded to follow you.'" A similar statement is His saying: "And we will not believe in your ascension until you send down to us a book that we may read" (17:93).

It is also said: they said, "If Muhammad is truthful, let there be in the morning, at the head of each man among us, a scroll in which is his acquittal and his safety from the Fire."

"Kallā" (ﷻ no) — a rebuke to them for that desire, and a deterrent against demanding signs. Then He said: ﴿Nay, but they do not fear the Hereafter﴾. Therefore they turned away from the Reminder, not because the giving of scrolls was impossible.

Surah 74, verse 54 in al-Nasafi's commentary (Madarik al-Tanzil):

﴿Nay, indeed it is a reminder.﴾ He restrained them from their turning away from the reminder, and said: indeed the Qur'an is a reminder that is eloquent and sufficient.
﴿So whoever wills, let him remember it﴾. That is: whoever wills to remember it, and not forget it, let him do so, for the benefit of that returns to him.

﴿وَما يَذْكُرُونَ﴾ ["And they do not remember"]. Nafi' and Ya'qub read it with the ta' (تَذْكُرُونَ, "you remember"), ﴿وَما يَذْكُرُونَ﴾ with the ta' instead of the ya'.

﴿إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللهُ﴾ ["unless God wills"]: that is, "except at the time of God's will," or "except by God's will."

﴿هُوَ أهْلُ التَقْوى وأهْلُ المَغْفِرَةِ﴾ ["He is worthy of being feared and worthy of forgiving"]. In the hadith: "He is worthy that He be feared, and worthy that He forgive whoever fears Him."
